exclusion_detail: Lead 4l is made by TBTU amide coupling of acid 1 with a tryptophan anilide 2l (3-bromophenyl), then ester -> hydroxamic acid with NH2OK. Procedures are given for those two steps (3x, 4x), but the tryptophan anilides 2a-2t are 'obtained following our team previously published methods' (ref 11) with no procedure here, and the source of acid 1 is not stated, so the route from commercial materials is not explicit.

lead.label: 4l
lead.why: Abstract: 'Among these analogs, 4l exhibited selectivity to HDAC1' (title is about HDAC1 inhibitors; Sec. 2.4 'with 4l being the most' selective; 4l is the compound docked into HDAC1). The abstract also lists 4h, 4i, 4j, 4l, 4r as superior to SAHA, so rule 1 is not unique; 4l is the only one the abstract singles out.

notes: Every target 4a-4w depends on an intermediate 2x prepared by reference only, so I found no compound with an explicit complete route. Numbering warning: the Experimental headings do not map cleanly to the text's labels (the text implies 4j = 4-Br with 4k/4l the ortho/meta isomers, whereas the heading order of the experimental section would put 2-Br and 3-Br at 4j/4k); the identity of 4l as the 3-bromo or 2-bromo anilide is therefore uncertain. Not material to this exclusion.
